issues_encountered: RUN_2026-04-25_07-28-05 (run 3): DRT-0074 persisted even after FP_IO_HLENGTH=4.0/FP_IO_VLENGTH=4.0 fix from run 2

True root cause: FP_IO_HTHICKNESS_MULT/VTHICKNESS_MULT left at default=2, yielding pin width 2*24=48 DBU. M4/M5 WIDTHTABLE requires 24, 120, 216... DBU; 48 DBU is NOT a valid width. Additionally, width=pitch=48 DBU means ~50% probability of zero on-grid tracks inside the pin rect depending on track grid offset at pin position. DRT 'Start pin access' phase aborts before detailed_route even runs — drt.tcl catch block does NOT help for this failure mode.

lessons_learned: Phase B1 hypothesis falsified: the resizer was NOT over-margined. After Phase A (Run 42) fixed CTS clustering and dropped setup buffers 299->124->84, all remaining timing-repair buffers are necessary repairs on paths with <75 ps slack. None were speculative repairs in the 75-100 ps window.

Margin reduction is only PPA-meaningful when paths exist in the slack range being cut. Run 43's path distribution clusters tightly behind the +5.97 ps WNS (per the campaign's known 'co-critical path exposure' lesson) - virtually no paths sit in 75-100 ps slack.

Power floor for this RTL/PDK with these floorplan parameters is locked at ~27.27 mW. Further power gains require RTL changes (more clock gating, datapath sharing) or PDK changes (mixed SVT/RVT - needs library availability check).

issues_encountered: Run 44 produced byte-for-byte identical PPA to Run 43. Resizer margin cuts from 100/150/100/100 to 75/75/50/50 had zero effect. Post-GRT resizer inserted same 84 setup buffers and 8 hold buffers regardless of the 25-50 ps margin reduction. Post-CTS resizer also unchanged (642 inserted, 182 hold buffers). Hypothesis was that 1500+ timing-repair buffers included over-margined redundant repairs; this was incorrect — the resizer is already working at the physical limit and the margin reduction was too small to change any insertion decisions.
lessons_learned: Resizer margin values are NOT a power-reduction lever at this design point. The margins were set to 0.100/0.150/0.100/0.100 in Run 38 to fight a logic-depth-limited path, but that path was closed by RTL changes and SDC uncertainty reductions in Runs 39-40. The margins were already irrelevant — the resizer inserts buffers because paths are close to failing (WNS +5.97 ps = only 6 ps headroom), not because of over-generous margins.
The 1559 timing-repair buffers are load-driven (cell fanout, wire RC) not margin-driven. Cutting margin from 100 ps to 75 ps does not eliminate buffers needed for capacitive load repair.

At +5.97 ps WNS with CTS skew 29 ps, the design is already at a local optimum for the current CTS structure. The only power lever remaining is to increase the clock period (reduce fmax) or add more structural clock gating.
Config-only power optimisation via resizer margins is PROVEN EXHAUSTED for this design.
